summary.headline: Granules Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR1,477 crore and PAT grew 60% to INR180 crore, with net debt/EBITDA at 0.07x.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 22% YoY to about INR14,768 million, broadly flat sequentially vs a strong Q4 FY26, led by finished dosages (complex generics) in North America and Europe. EBITDA rose 37% YoY to INR3,389 million at a 22.9% margin (down 99 bps QoQ), and PAT grew 60% to about INR180 crore. Operating cash flow jumped to INR3,874 million on a sharp receivables reduction in the US, and ROCE rose to 18%. Management said the Gagillapur (GGP) site remains the only facility without a clean FDA EIR, with 9 applications ready to launch once it clears.

segments.name: Finished dosages / complex generics
segments.commentary: Complex generics are about 50% of finished dosages, up from 39% a year ago; growth was supported by North America and Europe. Management did not disclose sub-segment growth within complex generics.

segments.name: Peptide CDMO (Senn, Zurich/Hyderabad)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about CHF5 million, up YoY but down QoQ after a strong Q4. Management said the segment's Q1 EBITDA was negative (about INR12 crore per an analyst's read, not disputed) due to project/product mix and long project cycles; FY27 target is PAT positive for the year. Revenue grew more than 100% over last year per the Chairman.

segments.name: API and oncology (Vizag)
segments.commentary: Oncology contribution so far is minimal; the first self-developed, fully backward-integrated oncology product is expected to launch in FY28/FY29. Company has 9 to 13 oncology products in development, and 2 ANDAs filed (one US, two European dossiers).

segments.name: GPI (US facility, Virginia)
segments.commentary: Received clean EIR in June; utilisation about 70%, with expansion needed by end FY28. Management describes it as low-volume, high-value output.

segments.name: Genome Valley (GLS)
segments.commentary: Adds about 40% to formulation capacity; utilisation is very low today and is expected to cross 50% by year-end FY27, with a 60% range also cited. Product extensions and some new filings were moved here as risk mitigation.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue growth to continue through FY27 but gave no numerical growth guidance.
EBITDA margin expected to stay in the 22% to 23% range (Chairman).
Remaining FY27 capex guided at about INR600 crore, with INR89 crore spent in Q1; capex to pick up on digitalisation and growth projects.

Peptide CDMO: target to be PAT positive for FY27 on an annual basis; medium-term goal of USD 50 million revenue at 30%+ EBITDA about mid-third year, and 5x revenue in 5 years. Management declined to give further numeric guidance.
About 9 US launches expected in FY27, pending FDA clearance of GGP; about 18 approvals pending in total.
R&D intensity expected at about 5.5% to 6% of sales going forward.
Working capital guided within the range given last quarter (about 33% of sales); receivable days may rise slightly as growth continues.
India peptide plans: about INR100 crore for intermediate and INR200 crore for API, not all to be spent in year one.
capex_capacity: Gagillapur (GGP) remediation described as essentially complete; FDA met in January 2026; no new product approvals from GGP until FDA visit and clearance. Seven of eight facilities now hold clean EIRs.
Genome Valley (GLS) completed; adds about 40% to formulation capacity; utilisation low, expected above 50% by year-end.

Zurich peptide upgrades: additional solid-phase reactors, large purification columns and lyophilisation capacity, with deliveries over the next few months; costs described as modest and largely pre-ordered.
Peptide India footprint: land earmarked at Vizag for a peptide facility; the next phase is initiated.
demand_pricing: Europe growth described as planned and driven by demand for previously filed products across API and finished dosages. Sequential softness in Q1 was attributed to intentionally holding supply on legacy-5 products due to cost pressure and pricing negotiations, plus pending controlled-substance approvals.

Raw material, packing, freight and supply-chain cost inflation from West Asia tensions; Q1 gross margin insulated by US opening inventory. Management is pursuing calibrated pricing and cost pass-through.

Controlled substances: 1 to 2 launches expected in FY28 (1.5 to 2 years out); 4 to 5 IP-based launches plus about 5 more pipeline products. No new controlled-substance launches in FY27. Granules is the fourth-largest US controlled-substance player.
Sodium oxybate filed as sole first-to-file; 2 sole first-to-file products in public domain with litigation expected.
Approvals pending: about 9 GGP facility-pending products with a combined market size of about USD 11 billion, plus about 9 IP-based products; in total about 23 to 24 filings pending.

qa_highlights.question: What growth can be expected in FY27 on a full-year basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said management is confident growth will continue at the current pace, without quantifying it.

qa_highlights.question: Total capex for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR600 crore remains for the rest of FY27 after INR89 crore spent in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Will the favourable complex-generics mix offset raw material pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman agreed RM pressures are high; mix shift to complex generics is expected to continue to help margins.

qa_highlights.question: Peptide CDMO: what milestone shows the platform is self-sustaining?
qa_highlights.answer: CSO cited USD 50 million revenue at 30%+ EBITDA around the middle of year three, with 3 customer wins of USD 10 million-plus annual size as proof points.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to a substantial cut in US receivable days, with inventory up only slightly and lower capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why was peptide CDMO EBITDA negative in Q1 (about INR12 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: CSO said there was no large one-off; it reflected project-to-product mix, quarterly opex variation and long project cycles, with some revenue carried into H2.

qa_highlights.question: What was remediation expense in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it was not significant, in line with recent quarters at less than USD 1 million per quarter; H1 FY26 was highest.

qa_highlights.question: GPI US facility utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said about 70%; products are low-volume, high-value, so this is not comparable to volume plants, with expansion needed by end FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company has been conservative so far, and internal discussion is under way on a possible increase.

risks_watch: Gagillapur FDA EIR still pending, which holds back 9 ready launches and new GGP approvals.
Raw material, packing and freight inflation from West Asia tensions could erode margins once US opening inventory is used up.
Peptide CDMO quarterly volatility: Q1 revenue fell QoQ and EBITDA was negative; management has not given numeric FY27 EBITDA guidance.
Controlled-substance launch timing is largely litigation-dependent (Dyanavel, Adzenys, others); no timelines disclosed.
Working capital could rise as receivable days normalise with growth; receivables fell sharply this quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins and cash generation, but cautious and evasive on specifics: management declined to quantify FY27 growth, peptide EBITDA and launch timelines, citing litigation and project lumpiness. Candour was highest on the Gagillapur remediation, where it acknowledged that approvals are paused until the FDA visit.

We are currently at around 70% capacity utilization.
So we have actually already ordered and the deliveries of these equipment, some of these missing in the infrastructure bouquet will happen over the next few months.
